questions.stem: What is the primary purpose of equivalence partitioning in test case design?

options.text: To test all possible inputs exhaustively.
To reduce the number of test cases by grouping similar inputs.
To ensure all branches of code are executed.
To test only the boundary values of input ranges.

questions.explanation: Equivalence partitioning aims to minimize the number of test cases by identifying groups of inputs that are expected to be treated similarly by the system. This helps in efficient testing without exhaustive input checking.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a key characteristic of boundary value analysis?

options.text: It focuses on testing the boundaries between partitions.
It ensures every line of code is executed at least once.
It uses test doubles to isolate units under test.
It tests only the most common input values.

questions.explanation: Boundary value analysis targets the edges of input ranges, as errors often occur at these boundaries. It is distinct from statement coverage and does not involve test doubles.

questions.stem: What does statement coverage ensure in the context of software testing?

options.text: Every possible input is tested.
Every line of code is executed at least once.
Every decision point is executed in all possible ways.
All boundary values are tested.

questions.explanation: Statement coverage ensures that each line of code is executed during testing. It does not guarantee that all decision branches or boundary values are tested.

questions.stem: Why might achieving 100% branch coverage still not guarantee a defect-free software?

options.text: Branch coverage does not test all possible input values.
Branch coverage only focuses on boundary values.
Branch coverage ensures all lines of code are executed.
Branch coverage includes testing of test doubles.

questions.explanation: Branch coverage ensures that all branches in the code are executed, but it does not account for all possible input values, which may lead to missed defects if certain input combinations are not considered.

questions.stem: A function accepts an integer input ranging from 1 to 100. Using boundary value analysis, determine the minimum number of test cases needed. Provide your answer as a whole number.
questions.explanation: Boundary value analysis suggests testing just below, at, and just above the boundaries. For the range 1 to 100, test cases should include: 0, 1, 2, 99, 100, and 101, totaling 6 test cases.

questions.stem: What role do mocks play in software testing?

options.text: They provide predefined responses to method calls.
They verify interactions between objects.
They ensure all code branches are executed.
They test the boundaries of input ranges.

questions.explanation: Mocks are used in testing to verify that certain interactions between objects occur as expected. They are distinct from stubs, which provide predefined responses.

questions.stem: For a function that processes input values from 1 to 50, how many equivalence partitions would you expect? Provide your answer as a whole number.
questions.explanation: Equivalence partitioning divides inputs into sets that are expected to be treated the same. Here, the partitions could be: less than 1, between 1 and 50, and greater than 50, resulting in 3 partitions.

questions.stem: Which coverage criterion is more comprehensive: statement coverage or branch coverage?

options.text: Statement coverage, because it executes every line of code.
Branch coverage, because it ensures all decision points are executed in all possible ways.
Both are equally comprehensive.
Neither, as they both have limitations.

questions.explanation: Branch coverage is more comprehensive than statement coverage because it requires that all possible branches at decision points are tested, not just that each line of code is executed.
